To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Dairy production is responsible for 2.4% of the world’s greenhouse gas (GHGs) emissions.

the climate change impacts on the dairy sector are likely to be small in comparison with other agricultural sectors, but that there is a need to reduce methane emissions to avoid the risk of a large negative impact on future production.

1) the climate change mitigation potential of dairy farms is substantial; and 2) the potential for dairy farms to reduce their GHG emissions depends on the level of ambition of the mitigation strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of climate smart dairy farming systems that will reduce the environmental impact of dairy production while maintaining the economic viability and social sustainability of the industry.
the following aspects of dairy farming: • Climate change and its impacts on dairy production and the dairy industry. •
understanding the role of dairy cattle in the global GHG budget and the development and implementation of strategies to reduce GHG emissions from the dairy sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
climate change is real, and that humans are contributing to the warming of our climate.
the dairy industry is a net contributor to greenhouse gas (CHG) emissions.
dairy cows do contribute to the global climate change, but not to a large extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an integrated approach for the mitigation of enteric CH4 in ruminants.
we have developed a method that can be used to determine methane emissions from dairy cows and that we have shown that the method works in a field setting and is repeatable.

the use of a combination of feed additives (e.g., ionophores and essential oils) in dairy cows can reduce methane production and increase milk yield, which can be a climate-smart strategy for dairy farming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dairy cows are an important source of GHG emissions, and there are a variety of management practices that can reduce these emissions.

the climate impacts of dairy production are not only due to the direct emissions from cows, but also due to the emissions from the production of feed, and the emissions from the processing and transportation of milk and dairy products to the consumer.
the methane emissions per kilogram of milk are similar for all dairy cows.
